project-oneliner: Your agents are grading their own homework — Keel measures how much.
project-description: Keel measures whether a codebase's verification actually touches the world, or whether it is only checking itself. A check is only a check if the signal it reads comes from somewhere the thing being checked cannot write to. Most verification in an agent-maintained codebase fails that test: an LLM reviews what an LLM wrote, a doc is validated against another doc, a status field reads 'passed' because something set it to 'passed'. The pipeline is green and nothing has been verified. Keel walks every verification edge in a target — CI steps, test targets, review gates, deploy conditions, integration signals — and classifies each as anchored (the producer sits outside the actor's write boundary), self-referential (it sits inside), or unknown (untraceable, and it fails closed). The result is a grounding ratio. Novel shapes are judged by the agent; recurring shapes are crystallized into probes — small reviewable scripts — so the next occurrence costs no model call, and the library compounds across everyone who runs it. Probes may abstain but may never return unknown, which keeps 'unknown' unshoppable by the thing being measured. Keel also audits itself: it re-decides a sampled fraction of probe-classified nodes agentically with the cached verdict hidden, and retires probes that disagree. Shipped as an open agent skill (npx skills add broomva/keel), so it runs inside any agent harness rather than reimplementing one. MIT.
